input.quote: 14.2 Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
input.rationale: Section 14.1 (Customer Data ownership, with Vendor's processing right confined to providing, securing, supporting and improving the Services for Customer), 14.3 (Vendor retains Vendor Technology; embedded Vendor Technology carried by the perpetual licence in 13.2) and 14.4 (no joint ownership) are all acceptable. Section 14.2, however, gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable we pay to have created and leaves us only a revocable, non-transferable licence lasting no longer than the Order Form term. That fails even the fallback, which requires a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense Deliverables — the 13.2 perpetual licence reaches only software and Vendor Technology, not the Deliverable itself. Because the remaining preferred elements are already satisfied elsewhere in Section 14 and 13.2, the shortest complete cure is to flip 14.2 to Customer ownership with an express assignment, reaching the preferred position in a single edit.

proposal.summary: Flip Deliverable ownership to Customer with an express assignment; Vendor keeps Vendor Technology under 14.3 and the perpetual embedded-IP licence in 13.2.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We own what we pay for, so we have reversed Section 14.2 to give Customer ownership of each Deliverable with an express assignment from Vendor, in place of the revocable, term-limited licence. Vendor still retains Vendor Technology under Section 14.3 and Customer's embedded-IP licence in Section 13.2 is unchanged.

ops.newText: Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer, and Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in each Deliverable.

mappings.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
mappings.quote: For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence

mappings.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
mappings.quote: Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.

mappings.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
mappings.quote: a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence

mappings.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
mappings.quote: As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services.

mappings.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
mappings.quote: No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.

mappings.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
mappings.quote: No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument identifying it and their exploitation rights.
